description: CANDIDATE DETECTOR WITH A DELIBERATELY SMALL EVIDENCE BASE, STATED AS SUCH. Mechanism: a TypeScript ignore comment in an authored test suppresses exactly the check that would have caught a reference to an interface that does not exist, so the error survives compilation, fails only at runtime, and then persists indefinitely because the compose verification gate is delta-aware and a failure already present in the baseline does not refuse a draft. CONCRETE INSTANCE: repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.test.ts contains sixteen ts-ignore comments and fails all four of its tests with TypeError undefined is not an object, because it reads resolveGapToFeature.gapComposeLastAttemptAt, a property the implementation never defines. Without the suppression, the compiler would have rejected that property immediately. EVIDENCE BASE AND ITS LIMITS: the vessel has 21 test files, of which 2 are substrate-authored. The substrate-authored file that uses ts-ignore has never passed; the substrate-authored file that does not, src/lib/stable-finding-id.test.ts, passes 10 of 10. That is a perfect but tiny correlation at n equals 2, and it is NOT sufficient to call this a recurring class. It is offered as a candidate detector, not an established one. PROPOSED DETECTOR, CHEAP AND MECHANICAL: flag any authored test file containing a TypeScript ignore or expect-error comment, and for each member access on an imported symbol in that file, check the accessed name against the module's actual exports and declared properties. This is the same shape as the anchor-provenance guard in edit-provenance.ts, which compares identifiers in a proposed replacement against the target module and was repaired earlier today. PROPOSED REPAIR GOAL GENERATION: when the detector fires, mint a goal to rewrite the test against an interface the module genuinely exposes, preferring an existing seam. In the concrete instance such a seam already existed and was ignored: requeueAfterNonAttempt is exported from gap-to-feature.ts with the comment Exported for unit test only and takes a fully injectable signature, so the behaviour was testable deterministically all along. EXECUTABLE CLOSURE CHECK: run the vessel test suite and assert that no test file both contains a TypeScript suppression comment and reports failures, and that every substrate-authored test file passes.
